questions.text: When a user drags a container element that has bound arrows or text, how does Excalidraw propagate the position update to those bound elements — which function computes the new binding-aware endpoint position for a bound arrow, and which separate function applies that computed point to actually move the arrow?

goldFacts.statement: dragSelectedElements, for each non-arrow element being dragged, calls updateBoundElements(element, scene.getElementsMapIncludingDeleted(), { simultaneouslyUpdated: ... }) after moving the element's coordinates, to keep its bound elements attached.
updateBoundElements returns immediately without doing anything if the changed element is not a bindable element (isBindableElement(changedElement) is false).

updateBoundElements uses boundElementsVisitor to visit elements bound to the changed element, but the visitor callback itself skips (returns early for) any element that is not a non-deleted linear element, and separately skips any bound element that doesNeedUpdate reports as not stale — only the remaining elements are actually repositioned.

updateBoundPoint(element, bindingProp, bindings[bindingProp], bindableElement, elementsMap) is the function that computes the new binding-aware endpoint position for a bound linear element's start or end point; it is called from inside the bindableElementsVisitor callback that builds the `updates` array.

For a bound linear element that is not simultaneously being updated itself, updateBoundElements takes the point(s) already computed by updateBoundPoint (the `updates` array) and calls LinearElementEditor.movePoints(element, updates, ...) to actually apply them and move the arrow's bound point(s).
If the bound linear element also has a bound text label, updateBoundElements calls handleBindTextResize(element, elementsMap, false) to keep that label positioned correctly after the reposition.

questions.text: When elements are deleted from the scene (e.g. via the Delete/Backspace action), how does Excalidraw clean up the bindings that referenced those now-deleted elements, so that surviving elements don't keep dangling references to elements that no longer exist?

goldFacts.statement: actionDeleteSelected's perform, after deleteSelectedElements produces the next element list, calls fixBindingsAfterDeletion(nextElements, nextElements.filter((el) => el.isDeleted)) to clean up bindings that referenced the just-deleted elements.

fixBindingsAfterDeletion, for each deleted element, calls BoundElement.unbindAffected(elements, element, mutateElement) to strip that deleted element's id out of the boundElements list of any bindable element (e.g. a container or arrow endpoint) it had been attached to.

fixBindingsAfterDeletion also calls BindableElement.unbindAffected(elements, element, mutateElement) for each deleted element, to null out the binding pointer of any surviving element that had been bound to it.

BoundElement.unbindAffected visits the deleted bound element's bindable elements and, for each one whose boundElements array still references the deleted element's id, calls updateElementWith to rewrite that array with the deleted element's id filtered out.

BindableElement.unbindAffected visits the deleted bindable element's boundElements and, for each surviving element bound back to it, calls updateElementWith to null out that element's binding property (e.g. containerId, startBinding, or endBinding) so it no longer points at the deleted element.

questions.text: Trace how an element in the scene actually gets drawn onto the canvas: which React component invokes the static-scene render function, and where does the rendering code obtain (or generate) the roughjs shape it draws?

goldFacts.statement: The StaticCanvas React component calls renderStaticScene(...) to draw the non-interactive canvas layer whenever its effect runs.

renderStaticScene, when called with throttle=true, delegates to renderStaticSceneThrottled and returns immediately, instead of falling through to the direct _renderStaticScene(renderConfig) call at the end of the function.
The internal static-scene render routine draws individual elements by calling renderElement for each one (one of several such call sites in the function).
renderElement (in renderer/renderElement.ts) calls ShapeCache.generateElementShape(element, renderConfig) to obtain the roughjs Drawable shape for the element before drawing it.
ShapeCache.generateElementShape returns the already-cached shape from its WeakMap without regenerating it, as long as a cached (non-exporting) shape is already present for that element.

questions.text: When a WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE message arrives over the collaboration socket, how does excalidraw-app merge the remote elements into the local scene, and what rule decides whether the local or the remote version of a conflicting element is kept?

questions.text: What are the variants of the ExcalidrawElement discriminated union, what type alias derives the set of each variant's literal type tag, and what do the boundElements and version fields (defined on every element's shared base type) represent?

goldFacts.statement: ExcalidrawElement is a discriminated union of ten element variants: generic, text, linear, arrow, free-draw, image, frame, magic-frame, iframe, and embeddable elements.
ExcalidrawElementType is derived from the union itself, as ExcalidrawElement["type"] — the set of each variant's literal type tag.
Every element's shared base type carries a boundElements: readonly BoundElement[] | null field listing the other elements that are bound to it.
Every element's shared base type also carries a version: number field, sequentially incremented on each change and used to reconcile elements during collaboration or when saving to a server.

questions.text: What MIME types do IMAGE_MIME_TYPES's svg, png, and jpg entries map to, and how does the general-purpose MIME_TYPES constant relate to the image-specific IMAGE_MIME_TYPES constant?

goldFacts.statement: IMAGE_MIME_TYPES.svg maps to the MIME type "image/svg+xml".
IMAGE_MIME_TYPES.png maps to the MIME type "image/png".
IMAGE_MIME_TYPES.jpg maps to the MIME type "image/jpeg".
MIME_TYPES.binary is defined as "application/octet-stream".
MIME_TYPES spreads all of IMAGE_MIME_TYPES into itself (...IMAGE_MIME_TYPES), so every image MIME type recognized by IMAGE_MIME_TYPES is also a valid MIME_TYPES value.

Excalidraw uses **soft deletion**: deleted elements stay in the elements array with `isDeleted: true` rather than being physically removed. So after a delete action, the app calls `fixBindingsAfterDeletion(sceneElements, deletedElements)` (in `packages/excalidraw/element/binding.ts:1519`) to strip out any references to those now-deleted elements from the survivors' binding fields.

`fixBindingsAfterDeletion` iterates the deleted elements and, for each one, calls two static helpers:

1. **`BoundElement.unbindAffected(elements, deletedElement, mutateElement)`** — treats the deleted element as something that *points at* bindable elements (via `containerId`, `startBinding.elementId`, `endBinding.elementId`). For each bindable element it points to (if that bindable element is itself still alive), it removes the deleted element's id from that bindable element's `boundElements` array.

2. **`BindableElement.unbindAffected(elements, deletedElement, mutateElement)`** — treats the deleted element as something that is *pointed at* by others (via its own `boundElements` list, e.g. bound text or arrows). For each surviving bound element listed there, it walks that element's own bindable references (`containerId`/`startBinding`/`endBinding`) and nulls out any that point back to the deleted element's id.

Both helpers rely on shared visitor functions (`boundElementsVisitor` and `bindableElementsVisitor`) that walk the four binding relationships (`frameId`, `containerId`, `startBinding`, `endBinding`, `boundElements`), and both explicitly skip elements that are themselves already `isDeleted` (no need to clean those, since they're gone too).

This is invoked from the delete paths:
- `actionDeleteSelected.tsx:275` — after soft-deleting the selection, calls `fixBindingsAfterDeletion(nextElements, nextElements.filter(el => el.isDeleted))`.
- `App.tsx:4923` — when a text element is emptied out and thus deleted (e.g. label/bound-text editing), it calls `fixBindingsAfterDeletion` for that single element.

So the cleanup is two-directional and symmetric: it removes the dangling id from `boundElements` arrays on bindable elements that used to be bound-to by something deleted, and it nulls out `containerId`/`startBinding`/`endBinding` on live elements that used to reference a now-deleted bindable element — ensuring no surviving element keeps a reference to an id that's gone.

## Merge flow

When a `WS_SUBTYPES.UPDATE` message arrives (`excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx:583`), `Collab` decrypts the payload and calls:

```ts
this.handleRemoteSceneUpdate(this._reconcileElements(decryptedData.payload.elements))
```

**`_reconcileElements`** (`Collab.tsx:733`) grabs the full local scene (`getSceneElementsIncludingDeleted()`), restores/normalizes the incoming remote elements via `restoreElements`, then calls the shared `reconcileElements` utility (`packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`) with `(localElements, remoteElements, appState)`. It also updates `lastBroadcastedOrReceivedSceneVersion` *before* applying the update, so the just-received scene isn't re-broadcast back to the room.

**`handleRemoteSceneUpdate`** then applies the reconciled result via `excalidrawAPI.updateScene({ elements, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER })` (so it doesn't get pushed onto the undo/redo history) and kicks off `loadImageFiles()`.

## Conflict resolution rule

`reconcileElements` walks each remote element and decides whether to keep the local copy or accept the remote one via `shouldDiscardRemoteElement` (`packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts:19`). The remote element is **discarded** (local kept) when a local element with the same id exists and any of:

- it's currently being actively edited locally (`editingTextElement`, `resizingElement`, or `newElement` matches the id), or
- `local.version > remote.version` (local is strictly newer), or
- `local.version === remote.version && local.versionNonce < remote.versionNonce` — a deterministic tie-breaker on equal versions, based on comparing the random `versionNonce`.

Otherwise the remote element wins and replaces the local one. Elements that exist only locally (not present in the remote payload) are appended afterward untouched. The final list is then reordered by fractional index (`orderByFractionalIndex`) and de-duplicated (`syncInvalidIndices`).

- **`handleRemoteSceneUpdate`** (`Collab.tsx:771`) then applies the reconciled element list to the local scene via `excalidrawAPI.updateScene({ elements, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER })` (so it doesn't get pushed onto the undo/redo history), and kicks off `loadImageFiles()` to fetch any new image assets referenced by the incoming elements.

## Merge algorithm (`reconcileElements` in `packages/excalidraw/data/reconcile.ts`)

For each remote element:
- If there's no local element with the same id, the remote element is added.
- If there is a local element with the same id, `shouldDiscardRemoteElement` decides whether to keep the **local** version instead of the incoming remote one. The local version wins (remote is discarded) if:
  - the local element is currently being actively edited (`editingTextElement`, `resizingElement`, or `newElement` matches its id), **or**
  - `local.version > remote.version` (local is strictly newer), **or**
  - `local.version === remote.version && local.versionNonce < remote.versionNonce` — a deterministic tie-breaker when both sides edited at the same version: the element with the **lower `versionNonce`** wins.
- Otherwise the remote element replaces the local one.

Any local elements not present in the remote payload are appended unchanged afterward. Finally, the merged list is reordered by fractional index (`orderByFractionalIndex`) and de-duplicated indices are synced (`syncInvalidIndices`) before being returned as the reconciled scene.

## The `ExcalidrawElement` union

Defined in `packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts:203-213`:

```ts
export type ExcalidrawElement =
  | ExcalidrawGenericElement   // selection | rectangle | diamond | ellipse
  | ExcalidrawTextElement
  | ExcalidrawLinearElement
  | ExcalidrawArrowElement
  | ExcalidrawFreeDrawElement
  | ExcalidrawImageElement
  | ExcalidrawFrameElement
  | ExcalidrawMagicFrameElement
  | ExcalidrawIframeElement
  | ExcalidrawEmbeddableElement;
```

`ExcalidrawGenericElement` (types.ts:178-182) is itself a sub-union of `ExcalidrawSelectionElement | ExcalidrawRectangleElement | ExcalidrawDiamondElement | ExcalidrawEllipseElement`, so the fully expanded set of variants is: selection, rectangle, diamond, ellipse, text, linear (generic line/draw), arrow, free-draw, image, frame, magicframe, iframe, embeddable. Each variant is `_ExcalidrawElementBase & { type: "<literal>"; ...extra fields }`.

## `boundElements` and `version` (on `_ExcalidrawElementBase`, types.ts:38-80)

- **`boundElements: readonly BoundElement[] | null`** — the other elements bound to this element (e.g. text labels bound to a container, or arrows bound to a shape). Each `BoundElement` is just `{ id; type: "arrow" | "text" }`, a lightweight reference rather than the full element.
- **`version: number`** — an integer sequentially incremented on every change to the element, used to reconcile elements during collaboration or when saving to the server (paired with `versionNonce`, a randomly regenerated tiebreaker used when two versions are identical).

`ExcalidrawElement` (`packages/excalidraw/element/types.ts:203`) is a union of 10 top-level members, each discriminated by a `type` string literal:

## `boundElements` and `version` (on `_ExcalidrawElementBase`, `types.ts:38`)

- **`boundElements`** (`readonly BoundElement[] | null`, line 74) — lists the other elements bound *to* this element (e.g. arrows/text bound to a shape), where `BoundElement` is `{ id: string; type: "arrow" | "text" }`. It's the reverse-reference side of element bindings (e.g. a shape knows which arrows/labels are attached to it).
- **`version`** (`number`, line 58) — an integer sequentially incremented on each change to the element, used to reconcile elements during collaboration or when saving/syncing with a server (paired with `versionNonce` for tie-breaking when two versions match).
